abstraction_design.rationale: The abstractions track the app's real variation (cards, sections, sortable tables, pokemon-ref lists) and stretch to similar cases with render props rather than flag creep. Small copy-paste (num, the four near-identical page shells) and the underused extra seam keep it at 4.

findings.issue: The Pokémon card object is built in two places with inconsistent sprite strategies: cardsFromPokemonRefs uses pattern-only spriteUrl(id), while getHomeData (data.js:176) prefers the API's front_default. A sprite or card-shape fix can land correctly in one and miss the other.
findings.suggestion: Extract a single buildCard(pokemon, extra) helper (or give cardsFromPokemonRefs a species-ref sibling) and have the home page use it, so sprite and card-shape logic has one implementation.

findings.issue: The app has zero devDependencies, no lint config, no type check (tsconfig.json declares strict:true but there are no .ts files and no script), and no tests of its own — every edit is verified only by the external acceptance suite.
findings.suggestion: Add an eslint (or tsc --noEmit with .ts sources) step and a smoke test; even a minimal 'npm run check' would catch orphaned exports and broken imports during removals.

findings.issue: getAbilityPage mutates cards after cardsFromPokemonRefs returns instead of using the extra seam that exists exactly for this purpose (the comment at data.js:389 even acknowledges it).
findings.suggestion: Pass an extra callback that captures the hidden flag per ref, keeping all per-card enrichment in the card builder.

findings.issue: The COLUMNS config drives only the header row; the tbody cell order and contents are hardcoded (props.method.hasLevel && …), so adding a column means editing COLUMNS, the thead loop and the row body in three coordinated spots within one file.
findings.suggestion: Drive both headers and cells from one column definition (key, label, render) so a column is added once.

findings.issue: The 'not-found vs content' page shell (<Show when={data() === null}><NotFound/></Show>… plus a Content subcomponent) is copy-pasted across four route files (types, moves, abilities, pokemon).
findings.suggestion: Extract a small DetailPage/ResourceRoute wrapper that takes the query accessor and a content component, as NotFound and Section already are.

findings.issue: num() (em-dash for missing values) is duplicated in moves/[name].jsx:11 and components/MoveTables.jsx:44; a change to how missing values render needs both.
findings.suggestion: Move num() into lib/util.js next to EM_DASH.

findings.issue: All six page queries plus every shared lookup live in one 450-line module, so every feature removal/addition touches this shared file.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable at this size; if it grows, split per-resource modules (lib/queries/pokemon.js etc.) that reuse apiFetch/apiList.

findings.issue: The #moves anchor jump is implemented with an onMount + window.location.hash read, which fights the browser's native anchor behaviour and only runs on client mount.
findings.suggestion: Rely on the native anchor (the section already has id="moves" at pokemon/[name].jsx:77) and drop the imperative scroll, or use scroll-behavior CSS.

summary: A well-layered, current-idiom SolidStart v2 app: thin routes, dumb components, one explicit server-query data module and single-implementation helpers for the spec's cross-cutting rules, so most changes are local and obvious. The main editability taxes are the duplicated Pokémon-card construction (two sites, two sprite strategies), the copy-pasted detail-page shells and num(), and the complete absence of in-app lint/type/test verification. All five scenarios resolve in one to three clearly located files, with the data-source change confined to a single function.

scenarios.notes: Delete the route directory, remove the contiguous Abilities section (pokemon/[name].jsx:89-102) and the contiguous getAbilityPage block (data.js:382-406). No nav link exists (app.jsx:14-17). Nothing catches a forgotten data.js export, so the last step relies on grep/diligence.

But the two producers use different strategies (pattern-only at :103 vs front_default-preferred at :176), so a fix that changes strategy must reconcile both sites in the same file.

If instead the default ordering changes, the sort lives in two producers in data.js (cardsFromPokemonRefs at :109-110 and the home page slice at :160), because default dex order is baked into the server queries.
